title: 🤖 GLM 5.4 arrives for Coding Plan subscribers — visual understanding, a million-token context, and a bigger quota!
body: 🤖 GLM 5.4 arrives for Coding Plan subscribers — visual understanding, a million-token context, and a bigger quota!

Chinese company Zhipu has launched its new model GLM 5.4 for all subscribers of the GLM Coding Plan, in a step that adds what the model was missing: the ability to see, along with a bigger usage quota and a longer context.

The biggest new thing in this release is that the model now understands images directly, after the previous model was text-only. A programmer can now attach a screenshot of an error, a drawing of an interface, or a technical diagram, and the model understands it and works with it as part of the coding task, without needing it described in words. The model works with a context window of up to one million tokens, letting it read entire software projects in one go.

The release also raised the weekly usage quota by 50 percent compared with the previous model, GLM 5.3, for subscribers on V2, V3, and Team plans. The model can be selected by the name glm-5.4 in supported coding tools, and as glm-5.4[1m] inside Claude Code for the full-context version.

The model relies on the "loop transformer" approach, which the company has expanded over the past three months, and says it delivers stronger coding performance overall than its predecessor. But the company has not yet published a full technical introduction, the model's parameter count, or official benchmark results, which means the final judgment on its real strength still awaits the numbers.
Simply put: a coding model that now sees the screen the way it reads code — will a screenshot become a replacement for explaining the problem?
If your model understands a photo of the error directly, do you still need to explain the problem in words?
